topics.guidance: Explain the prayer the way the chapter itself does — as shared heritage every GSEB child already owns from the school prાર્thana-sabha ('ગુજરાતની કોઈ પણ સ્કૂલના વિદ્યાર્થીઓને આ પ્રાર્થના મોઢે છે'); the loss in this scene is about memory and belonging, not about prayer meaning, so keep `explanation` there and anchor `real_life_example` on a school prarthana-sabha the child has stood in, never on what the prayer's words mean.

topics.guidance: Keep the five names exactly as the essay uses them — a shelf of Gujarati literary heritage the author fears will go unread — and state only that the chapter names them; add no biography, era, or devotional content about any of them that this page does not print.

topics.caution: The explanation could turn ગીતાજીનાં સ્થિતપ્રજ્ઞનાં લક્ષણો into an account of what સ્થિતપ્રજ્ઞ theologically means, when the chapter only runs it as one experiment showing that a language carries a feeling English does not.
topics.guidance: Keep `explanation` on the author's experiment itself — reading the same idea in Gujarati/Sanskrit versus English and noticing the difference in feeling ('દિલમાં અનેરાં આનંદ, શાંતિ, સાત્ત્વિકતાનો અનુભવ') — never on unpacking the Gita's teaching; `real_life_example` should stay inside a familiar language-feeling moment (a prayer, a lullaby, a school song heard in one's own tongue versus a translated one), never a scripture summary.

chapter_level.guidance: This નિબંધ leans on Hindu heritage material — the ઉપનિષદ પ્રાર્થના, ગીતાજીનાં સ્થિતપ્રજ્ઞનાં લક્ષણો, and the named bhakti-to-modern poets નરસિંહ-મીરાં-સુન્દરમ્-રાજેન્દ્ર-મકરંદ — purely as evidence for its language-and-culture argument.
